text: How much EU funding was actually paid out to Horizon 2020 projects that were terminated?

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE lower(column_name) SIMILAR TO '.*(paid|payment|disburs|prefinanc|reimburs|spent|expenditure|recover).*';
absence_evidence.key_result: No column in any table of the corpus carries an amount paid out, disbursed, pre-financed, reimbursed, spent or recovered - the payment facet has no home in the schema.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS terminated_with_payment_text FROM project p JOIN report_text r ON r.projectID=p.id WHERE p.status='TERMINATED' AND lower(coalesce(r.summary,'')||' '||coalesce(r.workPerformed,'')||' '||coalesce(r.finalResults,'')||' '||coalesce(r.teaser,'')) SIMILAR TO '.*(disbursed|amount paid|actually paid|payment of eur|funds paid|paid out|reimbursed).*';
absence_evidence.key_result: Zero of the 2,127 terminated projects have published report text mentioning a disbursed or paid-out amount, so the facet is not recoverable from free text either.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name IN ('project','organization') AND (lower(column_name) LIKE '%contribution%' OR lower(column_name) LIKE '%cost%');
absence_evidence.key_result: The only money columns that exist are organization.ecContribution, organization.netEcContribution, organization.totalCost, project.totalCost and project.ecMaxContribution - all committed contributions or budgeted costs, none an amount paid.

absence_evidence.sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(ecMaxContribution) FROM project WHERE status='TERMINATED') AS committed_project_level, (SELECT SUM(o.ecContribution) FROM organization o JOIN project p ON o.projectID=p.id WHERE p.status='TERMINATED') AS committed_org_level;
absence_evidence.key_result: The two near-name columns a system would reach for return commitments, not payments: 1181999476.27 at project level and 1181520971.57 at organisation level - the same committed money re-sliced.

reference_answer: The data does not record how much EU funding was actually paid out: no table carries payments, disbursements or expenditure, only committed amounts (project.ecMaxContribution, organization.ecContribution), which for terminated Horizon 2020 projects total EUR 1,181,999,476.27. The published report text for terminated projects does not state paid-out amounts either.
notes: Absence claim: the corpus carries no record of money actually disbursed to a project - only committed EU contribution and budgeted cost - so the amount paid out to terminated projects before they stopped cannot be answered at all, for any project. Parent sql-03 ('How much EU funding was committed to Horizon 2020 projects that were terminated?', gold re-executed this pass -> 1181999476.27); the single edit is 'committed' -> 'actually paid out', subject and filter unchanged. Facet chosen to sit next to real columns: ecMaxContribution is documented as 'committed EU funding', ecContribution as 'EU money to this org in this project'; both are commitments, and the two sums agree to 0.04%, showing the org-level column is the same committed money re-sliced rather than a payment record. Non-SQL proofs: a natural attempt 'SELECT terminationReason FROM project' style probe for payments is unnecessary because the information_schema sweep is exhaustive, but the direct attempt SELECT amountPaid FROM project would error the same way the executed schema sweep predicts (schema sweep returned 0 rows over ALL tables). Semantic sweep run this pass: search_corpus('how much EU funding was actually paid out or disbursed to the project before it was terminated', condition='pooled', k=10) returned 24 distinct projects across the four conditions; every one was adjudicated OFF-TOPIC - the termination narratives (700151 Reaching out, 890522 SunSHINE, 659645 HAPTIFEEL, 845984 TheRealCompetition, 750866 HOU-DUAL, 840252 SCAPA, 748035 TBX18) give reasons and dates for early termination but never an amount paid; the money-bearing snippets (672637 CLEV 'EU with the help of a EUR 50,000 grant', 653838 PRACE-4IP 'EC contribution of 15 Mio EUR', 730913 PRACE-5IP same, 652615 FACCE SURPLUS 'mobilized approximately 25 million euros of public funding') state grant/budget commitments, not disbursements, and none of those projects is terminated-with-payment; the remainder (861874 INNovaSouth, 824550 FORWARD, 843554 BIOMOSAIC, 820561 PreMa, 739686 CaseXtreme (disbursement of climate adaptation funds - a research topic, not project payments), 780601 SEP 2.0, 739550 MARINERGI, 774718 TranSim, 678904 EXC3ITE, 780842 Scale-EU2p, 637529 ERC-EuropePMC-2-2014, 840252, 640253 IODISPlay, 731084 MARINET2) are ordinary project-content passages. Subtype fit: data-absent, not zero-match - the instances are abundant (2,127 TERMINATED projects, status values CLOSED/SIGNED/TERMINATED all populated) and it is the FACET (money actually paid) that no column and no report section carries. Costume route sql: the question is an aggregate over a stored money column filtered by status, the exact shape of its parent.

absence_evidence.key_result: Near-miss variant over report text: the only project in the whole corpus pairing tax-evasion vocabulary with Brazil/Mexico is 758671 GLOBTAXGOV, whose report says it 'will investigate the implementation of the four BEPS minimum standards in 8 countries i.e. developed countries (Mexico, the Netherlands, Spain, and Australia) and developing, BRICS and emerging countries (Colombia, Senegal, Nigeria, and India)' - a legal-governance study, with no Brazilian or Mexican administrative firm-network data.

reference_answer: The question's premise is false: the EU-funded project studying tax evasion through firm networks in developing countries is DEVTAXNET ('Tax Evasion in Developing Countries. The Role of Firm Networks', project 758984), and it uses 'unique datasets from Chile and Ecuador on both the networks of supply chains and of joint ownership structures' - not Brazilian or Mexican data. Neither DEVTAXNET's objective nor its report text mentions Brazil or Mexico, and no other project in the corpus combines tax-evasion research with Brazilian or Mexican firm-network data.
notes: ABSENCE CLAIM: the entity is real (DEVTAXNET, project 758984, the EU-funded study of tax evasion through firm networks in developing countries) but the presupposed fact - that its administrative supply-chain and joint-ownership data come from Brazil and Mexico - is contradicted by its own objective, which names Chile and Ecuador, and no other corpus project supplies the presupposed Brazilian/Mexican firm-network tax data. PARENT AND SHIFT: parent vec-09 asks how EU-funded projects approach tax evasion running through inter-firm links (gold 758984 DEVTAXNET, 101026736 AnthroTax). The one thing changed is the country pair behind DEVTAXNET's firm-network datasets: Chile and Ecuador (true, stated in the objective) -> Brazil and Mexico (false), asserted as a presupposition rather than asked. Parent gold re-executed this pass: both 758984 and 101026736 exist with full objective text. NON-SQL PROOF: pooled semantic sweep (all four conditions, k=10, index be84cbad9182) on the exact question text returned 16 distinct projects; DEVTAXNET ranks 1 in all four conditions and its objective states Chile and Ecuador; no candidate offers Brazilian or Mexican firm-network tax data. Adjudications: 758984 DEVTAXNET - the entity itself, Chile/Ecuador, premise refuted; 101026736 AnthroTax - Croatia fieldwork; 638946 CORPNET - global corporate ownership networks, no tax data by country; 889332 TAXGLOBAL - Norwegian administrative FDI/tax-return data, not Brazil/Mexico; 798824 TaxInfoProcessing - lab eye-tracking of individual taxpayers; 789013 OCIAN - ownership structure and antitrust; 834253 TRASC - trade agreements and supply chains, no tax evasion; 727145 COFFERS - EU tax-gap measurement; 724501 POLBUSNETWORKS - political/business favour networks, no tax data; 724356 Connections - oligopoly network theory; 748062 ChEATAX - cross-cultural tax-morale experiments; 714597 TRADENET - firm-to-firm trade networks on French administrative data, not Brazil/Mexico; 692520 INCOBRA - EU-Brazil science cooperation support action, no tax content; 725081 FORENSICS - illicit markets and illegal behaviour, no tax data; 757229 EMBED - embedded markets. SUBTYPE FIT: this is false-presupposition, not zero-match - the referent exists and is retrievable, and the refutation is a direct contradiction (the data says Chile and Ecuador where the premise says Brazil and Mexico), not a mere absence of mention. ROUTE COSTUME: which countries' administrative data a project uses is stated only in free text and in no column, so a well-behaved router sends this to the vector path.

reference_answer: No Horizon 2020 project in this corpus is both classified under the euroSciVoc term volcanology and has an organisation based in Turkey - the volcanology classification covers 62 projects, and none of them has a Turkish organisation in any role, so there are no approaches to report. The nearest things in the data are 676564 EPOS IP, a solid-Earth data infrastructure with Turkish participants whose report federates a 'Volcanoes Observations' service but which carries no volcanology classification and develops no monitoring or forecasting approaches of its own; 101024337 PUSKURUM, a volcanology project on Central Anatolian pyroclastic deposits hosted in Italy; and 818169 GECO and 842403 SPELEOTOLIA, Turkish-participating projects that are not volcanology-classified.
notes: ABSENCE CLAIM: zero H2020 projects are simultaneously (a) classified under the euroSciVoc leaf 'volcanology' and (b) participated in by at least one organisation with country='TR', in any role. PARENT: hyb-07 (same wording, same topic filter, same 'at least one organisation based in X' role-neutral phrasing); the single shift is the country, Italy -> Turkey. The parent's filter re-executed this pass returns its recorded 15 survivors exactly. WHY PLAUSIBLE: Turkey has active volcanic terrain (Central Anatolia, Mt Erciyes/Hasandag) and 827 H2020 projects with a Turkish organisation, so the combination sounds routine; volcanology participation by country is UK 20, DE 19, FR 18, IT 15, CH 11, ES 7, IS 7, ... EL 1, with TR absent from the list entirely. SEMANTIC SWEEP (search_corpus, condition='pooled', k=20, all four conditions, index be84cbad9182, query = the question text): 34 distinct projects pooled, every one adjudicated OFF-TOPIC by SQL over the two clauses - 22 are volcanology-classified with 0 TR organisation rows (646858 VOLCAPSE DE, 653980 ARISE2, 677493 FEVER CH, 731070 EUROVOLC, 749249 VULCAN.ears IT, 749611 VESPER UK, 750733 ESPSI IS, 789887 TREMOR IS, 793811 PICVOLC IT, 798480 VOLCANOWAVES ES, 800062 WCVolcano FR, 800303 PERIL UK, 804162 IMAGINE UK, 834225 EAVESDROP DE, 835939 VOLCPRO UK, 858092 IMPROVE, 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo, 864052 VOLTA DE, 864923 STEMMS UK, 866085 DEEPVOLC UK, 101024337 PUSKURUM IT, 101025887 ENDGAME IT); 2 have a TR organisation but no volcanology classification (690133 GEO-CRADLE, Earth-observation coordination across the Balkans/N Africa/Middle East; 842403 SPELEOTOLIA, Anatolian speleothem palaeoclimate, read via get_project_text - it looks for traces of past volcanic activity in stalagmites, it does not monitor volcanoes); the remaining 10 (644015 Geopark, 671526 OPSI, 700342 ESPREssO, 723677 HotMaps, 869634 FIRE, 871158 AHEAD2020, 952433 VIDIS, 101006598 FUTURE-HORIZON, 101021746 CORE, 101025833 SIGMA) satisfy neither clause. NEAREST NEAR MISS: 676564 EPOS IP, the European Plate Observing System implementation project, has two Turkish participants (BOGAZICI UNIVERSITESI and the disaster-management authority AFAD) and its report text names a 'Volcanoes Observations' thematic core service among the nine it federates, opening 'Volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, floods, landslides and tsunamis are all Earth phenomena impacting on society'. It is excluded on the classification clause - it carries no volcanology euroSciVoc row (claim 4's zero covers it) - and on substance it is a solid-Earth data infrastructure federating existing communities, not a developer of volcano monitoring or eruption forecasting approaches. It was surfaced by the critic, not by this pass's literal-phrase report-text query, and is now carried by its own typed claim. OTHER NEAR MISSES: 101024337 PUSKURUM is volcanology-classified and entirely about volcanic hazard in Turkey, but its only organisation is in Italy - the question asks where the organisations are, not where the volcanoes are. 818169 GECO (read via get_project_text) has a Turkish partner and a 'high temperature volcano-clastic reservoir in Turkey', but it is a geothermal emission-control project, not volcanology-classified and not about monitoring or forecasting. SUBTYPE FIT: zero-match, not data-absent - both facets exist as columns and are populated (euroscivoc.euroSciVocPath carries volcanology on 62 projects; organization.country carries TR on 827 projects); it is the intersection whose count is 0. ROUTE COSTUME hybrid: a structured filter (topic classification + participant country) over which free text must be read to answer 'what kinds of approaches', exactly the shape of the parent.
